list.name: Binance
list.description: The largest exchange reserve on chain. Binance publishes its BTC proof-of-reserves addresses every quarter; the wallets below are those disclosures plus the BTCB reserve that backs its wrapped token.
list.extra: Sources: Binance quarterly proof-of-reserves (68 BTC addresses), the BTCB reserve announced on the Binance blog, and the Binance Pool reward address. Balances were read from mempool.space.

list.name: U.S. Government
list.description: Bitcoin held by U.S. federal agencies from seizures. Two wallets dominate: the 94,643 BTC recovered from the 2016 Bitfinex hack and the 69,370 BTC seized from James Zhong's Silk Road theft.
list.extra: Arkham puts total U.S. government holdings at ~325,400 BTC. The verified addresses here hold what the public record supports; the Oct 2025 Prince Group forfeiture (127,271 BTC) is at custody addresses DOJ has not published, and the 25 wallets named in the complaint (listed, currently 0) held it before the 2024 consolidation. A further ~33,000 BTC sits in agency wallets that analytics firms track but do not name.
list.reportedNote: Arkham attributes ~325,447 BTC to the U.S. government (Oct 2025). The tracked addresses below are what public records support; the 127,271 BTC Prince Group forfeiture sits at unpublished custody addresses.

list.name: Satoshi Nakamoto
list.description: Bitcoin's creator. The genesis coinbase and the first blocks are fixed in the chain, so the addresses below are facts rather than attributions.
list.extra: Patoshi Pattern: about 22,000 blocks (~1.1M BTC; Whale Alert 2020 estimated 1,122,693 BTC over 22,503 blocks) are spread across some 20,000 coinbase addresses. They are deliberately not swept: 20,000 lookups would only earn a rate limit. The badge marks the estimate, the held total adds it, and the verified part is printed beside it.

est.label: Patoshi Est.
est.note: ~1,100,000 BTC: the rounded figure for the Patoshi pattern (Whale Alert 2020 counted 1,122,693 BTC over 22,503 blocks). An estimate from a named source, not a read balance.

addresses.label: Genesis block (block 0) coinbase
addresses.note: The 50 BTC of the genesis coinbase are unspendable by protocol and are not counted in address statistics. The balance shown is later donations only.

addresses.label: Block 1 coinbase (first block mined after genesis)
addresses.note: The address API reports 1.35275617 BTC received later, but the 50 BTC P2PK coinbase output of tx 0e3e2357... is still unspent, so the tracked balance is adjusted to 51.35275617 BTC. p2pkSats carries the 50 BTC the API leaves out, and a live read adds it back. This address is block 1, not block 9 (a common web error).

addresses.label: Block 9 coinbase (input of the first P2P transfer in block 170)
addresses.note: The original 50 BTC was spent as the input of the first person-to-person transfer (10 BTC to Hal Finney, block 170). The remainder is later donations.
